artifacts.summary: Fixed persisted-counter mint, authored regression suite, registered in manifest; deploy deferred to operator.

completion_data.completion_summary: Fixed skill_orchestrate_mint_dispatch_seq() in scripts/skill-base.sh to derive the minted dispatch_seq value exclusively from the loop guard file's persisted .dispatch_seq_counter rather than an ambient shell variable, closing the fresh-shell/fresh-subprocess re-mint defect. Authored and manifest-registered a new six-case regression suite (test-mint-dispatch-seq.sh) that reproduces the defect and demonstrably fails against the pre-fix body. Deploy propagation and full-suite discovery were deliberately deferred to the operator, per an explicit delegation-context safety constraint protecting a live /orchestrate loop currently depending on the deployed copy.

memory_candidates.content: When a shell function's committed source-store edit fixes a bug also present in a currently-deployed copy that a LIVE running process depends on mid-flight (e.g. an in-progress /orchestrate loop sourcing .claude/scripts/skill-base.sh), do not run the deploy step within the same dispatch that authored the fix. Verify suite logic against the fixed source-store body via a resolution-override scratch copy (temporarily pointing a copied test file's deploy-tree-first candidate at a nonexistent path so it falls through to the source-store file) instead of redeploying. Defer the actual deploy-headless.sh run and post-deploy verification to the operator, and record the deferral as a plan Phase's [COMPLETED WITH EXCLUSIONS] with a Reasoned Exclusions table naming the root cause and resolution path.

For a regression suite meant to prove a fix discriminates buggy-vs-fixed behavior, the mandatory red-demonstration can be done by reconstructing the exact pre-fix function body verbatim via `git show <prior-commit>:<path>` (sliced to the relevant line range) into a scratch shim file, then re-running the suite's own case logic against that scratch shim (via a temporary resolution override) rather than reverting the real repository. This proves the suite is discriminating without ever leaving the repo in a broken state.

To confirm a shell-suite failure is pre-existing and unrelated to a current change (rather than a regression introduced by it), create a throwaway `git worktree add <path> <pre-change-commit> --detach`, symlink the real (gitignored) deployed .claude/ directory into that worktree, run the same suite there, and compare results. Clean up with `git worktree remove --force` afterward. This lets baseline comparison happen without stashing or reverting any uncommitted work in the primary checkout.
